groups.problem: Delete puts the base logger into the context instead of the logger enriched with request fields.
groups.rationale: Both identify the same incorrect argument to klog.NewContext at line 97 and propose the same replacement.

groups.problem: Create and Update record Storage failures using the legacy duration recorder.
groups.rationale: The same incorrect recorder call appears in both Storage error branches. Each requires replacing recordLegacyDuration with recordStorageDuration.

groups.problem: Delete records successful Storage operations with the object name in the kind metric label.
groups.rationale: Both identify the name argument at line 106 and require replacing it with options.Kind.

groups.problem: The write tests do not synchronize with and verify their asynchronous legacy operations.
groups.rationale: All four tests assert only the Storage result and would pass if their legacy operation were removed. Each needs synchronization and an assertion that the legacy call occurred.

groups.problem: DeleteCollection records the legacy operation using the Storage duration recorder.
groups.rationale: All three identify the same recorder call after Legacy.DeleteCollection and propose recordLegacyDuration.

groups.problem: Logging and metrics dereference potentially nil options pointers without guards across the Mode3 methods.
groups.rationale: Both report the repeated unguarded access to options fields and propose guarding or defaulting those accesses.

groups.problem: Asynchronous legacy operations inherit request-context cancellation despite their ten-second timeout.
groups.rationale: Both report the same context-parenting mistake across the four asynchronous write paths and propose detaching cancellation.

problems: Create and Update attribute Storage failures to legacy metrics.
Delete uses the object name as the kind label for successful Storage operations.
DeleteCollection attributes its legacy operation to Storage metrics.
Fire-and-forget replication returns success before legacy persistence completes, changing the completion contract.
Legacy failures lose their previous error logging and are recorded only as metrics.
Asynchronous legacy operations inherit cancellation from the request context.
uncoveredProblems: Fire-and-forget replication no longer guarantees legacy persistence before returning success.
Legacy failures are no longer logged and are visible only through metrics.
